issues: Dolphin interior is filled with a coarse, uniform checkerboard dither that reads as a flat CAD fill rather than a volumetric lit-phosphor body; it lacks the rim-light-to-core brightness gradient the reference demands.
Dolphin silhouette proportions are off: the body is too thick/blunt through the midsection and the tail fluke is not clearly resolved as a fluke, weakening the graceful leaping arc.
Extra telemetry text in the bottom-right (128BPM / PHR / MEM) is not part of the reference layout and its bright cyan pulls the eye away from the dolphin, breaking the intended hierarchy.
VU-meter blocks in the bottom-left are more saturated/brighter than the subordinate FFT, creating an unbalanced hot spot in a corner that should be quiet.
No visible persistence/afterglow trail behind the dolphin, so the OEL phosphor-persistence character is not conveyed even though there is no foggy smear either.
suggestions: Replace the uniform dither fill on the dolphin with a directional brightness gradient (bright crisp rim light, dimmer dithered core) so it reads as a glowing 3D phosphor object instead of a flat shape.
Refine the dolphin outline: slim the torso, sharpen the tail fluke and pectoral fin, and smooth the arc so the silhouette is unmistakably a graceful leaping dolphin at 320x128.
Remove or strongly dim the bottom-right BPM/PHR/MEM telemetry text so the eye travels dolphin -> top track text -> waves -> FFT as specified.
Add a short, clean persistence trail (1-2 fading ghost frames) behind the dolphin to evoke real OEL phosphor decay without introducing whole-scene fog.
Lower the brightness/contrast of the bottom-left VU blocks to match the low-contrast FFT, keeping the entire bottom strip subordinate to the dolphin.
